title: Evidence-Based Reading — The Night Shift
description: Practice choosing the sentence that best supports an answer.
subject: rla
passage: Maria had worked the night shift at the packing plant for six years. She liked the quiet of it — the hum of the conveyor belts, the empty parking lot, the way the sky turned from black to gray just as her shift ended. Her coworkers came and went, chasing daytime hours and better pay, but Maria stayed. She told her sister it was because night shift paid a premium, but the truth was simpler: she had never learned to sleep well in daylight, not since she was a child.

questions.prompt: What is the best description of Maria's feelings about the night shift?

options.text: She resents it but has no other choice.
options.whyWrong: The passage does not show resentment; instead, it shows she likes several parts of the night shift and chooses to stay.

options.text: She has grown to prefer it.

options.whyWrong: She is not neutral. The details suggest a preference, not simple indifference.

options.text: She is actively trying to leave it.
options.whyWrong: Nothing in the passage shows she is trying to leave. In fact, others leave while she remains.

questions.explanation: The passage describes her enjoying the quiet and choosing to stay while others leave.
questions.rule: When the question asks about a character’s feelings, combine the descriptive details and the character’s actions rather than focusing on one isolated sentence.

questions.prompt: Which sentence from the passage best supports the idea that Maria's real reason for staying isn't about money?

options.text: She liked the quiet of it — the hum of the conveyor belts, the empty parking lot...
options.whyWrong: This helps show she likes the night shift, but it does not directly prove that money is not the real reason.

options.text: Her coworkers came and went, chasing daytime hours and better pay, but Maria stayed.
options.whyWrong: This compares Maria with her coworkers, but it does not directly reveal the truth behind her stated reason.

options.text: She told her sister it was because night shift paid a premium, but the truth was simpler.
Maria had worked the night shift at the packing plant for six years.
options.whyWrong: This is simply background information and does not address why she really stays.

questions.explanation: This sentence directly contrasts what she tells others with 'the truth,' signaling the stated reason isn't the real one.
questions.rule: For evidence questions, choose the sentence that directly proves the claim rather than one that merely relates to the topic.
questions.evidenceExcerpt: “She told her sister it was because night shift paid a premium, but the truth was simpler...” This is the exact line that signals money is not the real reason.
